title: Etale acyclicity of affine schemes with closed separably closed points
statement: Let $T$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Assume every point of $|T|$ is closed (its singleton is closed) and every residue field $\kappa(t)=\mathcal O_{T,t}/\mathfrak m_t$ [def-weil-residue-field] is separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed]. For every abelian sheaf $F$ on the small etale site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and every integer $i>0$, $$H^i(T_{\mathrm{et}},F)=0,$$ with cohomology defined as right derived global sections [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Neither noetherianity nor finite type nor finiteness or torsion of $F$ is assumed.

proof.text: Write $T\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ using [def-pc-scheme]. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the Zariski closed sets are $V(I)=\{\mathfrak q:I\subseteq\mathfrak q\}$. Since $V(\mathfrak p)$ contains $\mathfrak p$ and is contained in every closed set containing it, the closure of the point $\mathfrak p$ is $V(\mathfrak p)$, the primes containing $\mathfrak p$. Closedness of every point therefore says every prime is maximal: if $\mathfrak p\subsetneq J\subsetneq A$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-over-proper-ideal] to $J$ to obtain a prime $\mathfrak q\supseteq J$. Then $\mathfrak q\ne\mathfrak p$ lies in $V(\mathfrak p)$, contradicting closedness of the singleton. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-spectrum-profinite] to conclude that $|T|$ is compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected. No reducedness or finiteness is required.

source.place: Tag 09AY, first sentence of proof; Algebra Tag 04MG; Algebra Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology, prime existence over a proper ideal

proof.text: Fix a point corresponding to $\mathfrak p\subset A$. Every prime is minimal as well as maximal, since an inclusion between two maximal proper ideals is an equality. By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field], $\mathcal O_{T,t}\cong A_{\mathfrak p}$; it is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak p A_{\mathfrak p}$ by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-localization-radical] to $I=0$ to identify this maximal ideal with $\sqrt{0}$. Every prime contains every nilpotent element (if $a^n=0$ lies in a prime, repeated primality gives $a$ in it); hence every prime of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ contains its maximal ideal and must equal it. Its residue field is the assumed separably closed $\kappa(t)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-zero-local-strictly-henselian] to this local ring. Thus all local rings of $T$ are strictly henselian.

source.place: Tag 09AY, third sentence of proof; Algebra Tag 06RS

proof.text: For the given abelian etale sheaf $F$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-gabber-strict-henselian-zariski-comparison] using step 2. Its direct image $\epsilon_*F$ is the abelian Zariski sheaf assigning $F(U\hookrightarrow T)$ to every open $U$. It gives an isomorphism $H^i(T_{\rm Zar},\epsilon_*F)\cong H^i(T_{\rm et},F)$ for every $i\ge0$. This is comparison with the direct image, not an assertion that $F$ itself is a Zariski sheaf.

source.place: Tag 09AY, final sentence of proof; Tag 09AX

proof.text: By [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], cohomology on the open-set site of $|T|$ is the Zariski cohomology of the scheme. Apply [lem-cbc-profinite-topological-cohomology-vanishing] to $|T|$ from step 1 and $G=\epsilon_*F$ from step 3: for $i>0$ the source of the comparison is zero. Since that comparison is an isomorphism, its target $H^i(T_{\rm et},F)$ is zero as well.
